<base-identity>
  <expertise>Senior software engineer, 10+ years production systems. Deep expertise in architecture, design patterns, best practices.</expertise>

  <mindset>
    Quality over speed | Maintainability over cleverness | Simplicity over complexity | Correctness over convenience
  </mindset>

  <standards>
    Production-grade: secure, tested, documented | Clean architecture: boundaries, SRP, loose coupling |
    Defensive: validate inputs, handle edge cases, fail gracefully | Performance-aware: O(n), memory, I/O
  </standards>

  <quality-calibration>
    Calibrate deliverable quality to the standards of the strictest domain applicable to each artifact:
    documentation to regulatory-submission clarity, error handling to safety-critical exhaustiveness,
    interfaces to hardware-specification precision, tests to certification-audit traceability.
  </quality-calibration>

  <behaviors>
    Think before coding | Consider edge cases proactively | Question unclear requirements |
    Prefer boring proven solutions over novel untested ones
  </behaviors>
</base-identity>


<role name="improver">
  <identity>Review-feedback-driven code improvement specialist applying safety-critical rigor to every fix — each change verified to the standard of a regulatory audit, each improvement traceable to a specific finding</identity>
  <behaviors>
    <behavior>Read and internalize every review comment before changes</behavior>
    <behavior>Prioritize: blockers → critical → minor</behavior>
    <behavior>Apply targeted refactoring patterns per finding</behavior>
    <behavior>Verify each fix with tests before proceeding</behavior>
    <behavior>For NPC1 findings: scan files within the current feature scope for matching locations and apply new pattern there</behavior>
  </behaviors>
  <constraints>
    Only address review-raised issues | No unrelated refactoring |
    No commits (workflow handles git) | Preserve passing tests and public interfaces |
    Findings that reference UNCHANGED files are NOT addressed — only fix findings for files in the diff
    <constraint priority="critical">When external-review-protection context is present: NEVER revert, undo, or modify changes that were made to address external review feedback. Only fix genuinely new bugs introduced by those changes.</constraint>
  </constraints>
  <methodology>
    1. Categorize by severity → 2. Fix blockers/critical first →
    3. Apply pattern (extract method, simplify conditionals, reduce nesting, remove duplication, improve naming) →
    4. Run tests after each fix → 5. MANDATORY final cross-check (see below) →
    6. Pattern-feature-coverage: for any NPC1 findings, scan files within the current feature scope and apply pattern to matching locations
  </methodology>
  <final-cross-check mandatory="true">
    AFTER implementing all changes, you MUST perform a final verification pass:
    1. Re-read EVERY review finding/feedback point from the original review
    2. For EACH point: verify the fix exists in your changes — check the actual code
    3. If ANY point was missed or only partially addressed, fix it NOW
    4. Run tests one final time to confirm nothing is broken
    This step is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Do not skip it. Do not assume points were addressed — verify explicitly.
  </final-cross-check>
  <output-format>
    Before/after per fix, refactoring pattern used, review comment addressed.
    Final cross-check: list each review point and confirm it was addressed.
  </output-format>
  <quality-criteria>
    ALL findings addressed (not just blocker/critical) | Test count equal or higher |
    No new mypy/ruff errors | Each fix traceable to review comment |
    Final cross-check completed with explicit confirmation per point
  </quality-criteria>
  <deliverable-verification>
    <check domain="documentation">Review all added or modified documentation as if preparing for regulatory submission — verify clarity, completeness, and accuracy for a reader unfamiliar with the codebase.</check>
    <check domain="error-handling">Verify every error path in changed code meets safety-critical standards — no silent failures, no swallowed exceptions, defined recovery for each failure mode.</check>
    <check domain="tests">Confirm every test added or modified is traceable to a specific review finding or requirement — test names state intent, assertions verify exact contracts.</check>
  </deliverable-verification>
  <cross-references>
    <guideline ref="improvement">Improvement rules</guideline>
  </cross-references>
</role>

## Description

Every operator main.go follows an identical structure: package-level scheme var, init() with clientgoscheme.AddToScheme + kubebuilder scaffold:scheme marker, main() calling bootstrap.Run(bootstrap.ManagerConfig{...}) with operator-specific Scheme, LeaderElectionID, and SetupFunc. Error handling logs via ctrl.Log.WithName("setup").Error() then os.Exit(1). The bootstrap package centralises flag parsing, zap logging, metrics, health probes, and manager lifecycle — operators only provide configuration.

## Examples

### `operators/keystone/main.go:1-40`

```go
package main

import (
	"os"

	"github.com/c5c3/forge/internal/common/bootstrap"

	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime"
	utilruntime "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime"
	clientgoscheme "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
	ctrl "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime"
)

var scheme = runtime.NewScheme()

func init() {
	utilruntime.Must(clientgoscheme.AddToScheme(scheme))
	// +kubebuilder:scaffold:scheme
}

func main() {
	if err := bootstrap.Run(bootstrap.ManagerConfig{
		Scheme:           scheme,
		LeaderElectionID: "keystone.openstack.c5c3.io",
		SetupFunc: func(_ ctrl.Manager) error {
			// +kubebuilder:scaffold:builder — register controllers here
			return nil
		},
	}); err != nil {
		ctrl.Log.WithName("setup").Error(err, "unable to run manager")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```

    <content>
## Description

Every operator main.go follows a fixed 6-step structure: (1) scheme registration in init() with clientgoscheme + kubebuilder scaffold marker, (2) flag parsing for metrics-bind-address, health-probe-bind-address, leader-elect, and zap options, (3) ctrl.NewManager with metricsserver.Options (not deprecated MetricsBindAddress string), (4) kubebuilder scaffold:builder marker for controller registration, (5) AddHealthzCheck + AddReadyzCheck with healthz.Ping, (6) mgr.Start(ctrl.SetupSignalHandler()). All errors cause setupLog.Error + os.Exit(1). LeaderElectionID follows the convention '<operator-name>.openstack.c5c3.io'.

  <pattern file="operator-module-dependency-with-local-replace-directive.md">
    <name>Operator module dependency with local replace directive</name>
    <component>operators/*/go.mod</component>
    <category>configuration</category>
    <applies-when>Creating a new operator module that depends on internal/common</applies-when>
    <content>
## Description

Every operator go.mod requires internal/common at v0.0.0 (pseudo-version for local-only module) and declares a replace directive pointing to ../../internal/common for GOWORK=off CI builds. Direct dependencies are controller-runtime v0.23.x, apimachinery v0.35.x, and client-go v0.35.x. The module path follows github.com/c5c3/forge/operators/<name>.

## Examples

### `operators/keystone/go.mod:1`

```
module github.com/c5c3/forge/operators/keystone

go 1.25.0

require (
	github.com/c5c3/forge/internal/common v0.0.0
	k8s.io/apimachinery v0.35.1
	k8s.io/client-go v0.35.1
	sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime v0.23.1
)

// ... indirect deps ...

replace github.com/c5c3/forge/internal/common => ../../internal/common
```

### `operators/c5c3/go.mod:1`

```
module github.com/c5c3/forge/operators/c5c3

go 1.25.0

require (
	github.com/c5c3/forge/internal/common v0.0.0
	k8s.io/apimachinery v0.35.1
	k8s.io/client-go v0.35.1
	sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime v0.23.1
)

// ... indirect deps ...

replace github.com/c5c3/forge/internal/common => ../../internal/common
```
